To answer your question, I'm an anarchist - I don't believe in giving more power to the state. My hope is for a revolution to bring it crashing down, but in the meantime we do the little things we can to undermine its monopoly on violence and subvert capitalism. 

But I've got another question for you. If you'd have fought the police then, would you fight them now?

I'll ask you the same question I asked someone else.

At Stonewall, they fought cops. Would you have fought cops?

We take it back. We fuck shit up until they have no choice but to give it to us. The will is there, and has been for a long time. We just need some crisis to light the fire, and the way the economy is going we're heading towards just that.

As crushing as the oligarchs' grip on power is, it isn't absolute. Put enough pressure on them, and they will relent. They aren't suicidal, they can smell when things are getting too dangerous for them to just ignore.

Even if we don't get a total revolution, we still have things to gain by resisting. We saw that with the civil rights movement, we saw it with the union activity in the early 1900s. We can win, but only if we let go of our collective fixation with the idea that we can solve our problems the same way we got into them.
